forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Forest of Dean's budget strategy shows a £3.327m cumulative gap from 2027/28 to 2030/31
news_drafts.lead:
Forest of Dean District Council's budget strategy for 2027/28, before its Cabinet on 5 November, restates the council's medium term financial strategy, its multi-year budget forecast. The strategy shows a balanced budget for 2026/27, then annual funding gaps of £0.508m in 2027/28 and £0.686m in 2028/29. The gaps are £1.411m in 2029/30 and £0.722m in 2030/31, a cumulative £3.327m. The paper takes the February 2026 forecast as the starting point for 2027/28 and says the figures will be updated as detailed budgets, funding information and deliverable savings proposals are developed.

The council's Future Deficits Reserve stood at £874,957 on 1 April 2026. The paper says it "may provide short-term support, but it is not a permanent solution to the structural funding gap." Total reserves at that date were £13.4m, including a General Fund balance of £1.015m.

The paper also gives the February 2026 forecast as a cumulative gap of £4.616m over five years. It says the funding position may show a slight improvement, but that "there are a number of items that still need clarifying in order to confirm this." The paper's own figures in section 5.4 total £3.327m, and it does not reconcile that with the £4.616m. A review of balances and reserves will go to Cabinet and Council in December, alongside the 2027/28 budgets.

news_drafts.headline: Forest of Dean council improves forecast but faces £3.3m five-year funding gap
news_drafts.lead: Forest of Dean Council's medium-term financial strategy (MTFS), the council's financial plan for the next three to five years, shows a forecast funding gap of approximately £3.3 million over five years to 2030/31, an improvement from the £4.6 million gap identified previously. The council achieved a balanced budget for 2025/26, but the local government auditor's annual report notes the council will face a funding gap from 2027/28 onwards. The auditor says the council will need further savings, transformation activity and income generation to ensure long-term financial sustainability.
news_drafts.paper_title: F.794 Annex B FoDDC Agreed Actions Sept 2026

findings.headline: The paper gives the February 2026 forecast as a cumulative gap of £4.616m over five years and says the funding position may show a slight improvement, subject to clarifying several items.
findings.detail: The paper's own MTFS figures in section 5.4 total a cumulative gap of £3.327m, and the paper does not reconcile that figure with the £4.616m comparison. It says the improvement cannot be confirmed until a number of items are clarified.
findings.matters: Two different cumulative gap figures for the same MTFS period are something a finance director or lender would want reconciled before relying on either.
findings.figures: cumulative gap £4.616m over 5 years (February 2026 forecast, as cited); cumulative gap £3.327m (MTFS, section 5.4)
findings.quote: there are a number of items that still need clarifying in order to confirm this.

findings.headline: The paper assumes Council Tax base growth of 1.25% per annum from 2027/28 and says Council Tax and Business Rates assumptions will be updated for the latest tax-base forecasts and collection performance.
findings.detail: The Council Tax increase assumption is expected to stay at 3% or £5, whichever is greater, under the three-year settlement announced in December 2025. The paper says these assumptions will be checked against referendum principles before the final budget.
findings.matters: Tax-base and collection assumptions drive the income side of the gap, and a council revisiting them signals how far its income forecasts may move.
findings.figures: Council Tax base growth 1.25% per annum; Council Tax increase 3% or £5, whichever is the greater
findings.quote: Council Tax and Business Rates assumptions will be updated for the latest tax-base forecasts, collection performance, government policy and business rates retention arrangements.

findings.headline: The 2027/28 budget will include the anticipated financial implications of Local Government Reorganisation, including transition capacity and programme costs, with any government support recognised only when confirmed.
findings.detail: The paper does not quantify the LGR costs. It says the budget will also maintain financial resilience ahead of any successor arrangements, and it lists the future of Publica and other shared services among the drivers of the plan.
findings.matters: Reorganisation transition costs with no quantified figure yet are a risk that peer councils and lenders will want to see priced once the budget is set.
findings.quote: The 2027/28 budget will include the anticipated financial implications of Local Government Reorganisation, including transition capacity, programme costs and the need to maintain financial resilience ahead of any successor arrangements.

findings.headline: The Future Deficits Reserve stood at £874,957 on 1 April 2026, and the paper says it 'may provide short-term support' but 'is not a permanent solution to the structural funding gap'.
findings.detail: The paper lists total reserves of £13,368,728 at 1 April 2026, including a General Fund balance of £1,015,236. A review of balances and reserves will be presented to Cabinet and Council in December alongside the 2027/28 budgets.
findings.matters: A council stating that a reserve is not a permanent answer to its structural gap lets a reader see how far the position depends on one-off balances.
findings.figures: Future Deficits Reserve £874,957; total reserves £13,368,728; General Fund balance £1,015,236 (all at 1 April 2026)
findings.quote: The Future Deficits Reserve may provide short-term support, but it is not a permanent solution to the structural funding gap.

findings.headline: Forest of Dean reports it has delivered 'a number of budget and efficiency savings' and achieved income generation against its Savings Plan, with planned savings and additional income of approximately £1.583m over the MTFS period.
findings.detail: The paper says the Savings Plan will be refreshed with owners, delivery dates, recurring values and risk ratings. It also says the Council will need to review the adequacy and composition of the plan and is likely to need further savings beyond those already in the MTFS.
findings.matters: It shows a council reporting delivered savings alongside a plan it says must be strengthened, which is the gap between achieved and required recurring savings that finance teams and lenders track.
findings.figures: approximately £1.583m (planned savings and additional income over the MTFS period)
findings.quote: Whilst the Council has delivered a number of budget and efficiency savings and achieved income generation against its Savings Plan, the Council will need to review the adequacy and composition of the Savings Plan.
